transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me a little bit about what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because my body just feels completely drained. It's like... I don't know, even just walking from my car into the clinic today took everything I have. And at work, just sitting there and opening the EHR system feels like it takes all my energy. I just have nothing left in the tank.
Beyond the physical exhaustion you've described, have you been feeling persistently sad, low, or empty lately?

Yeah, I have. After all that energy I had just... dropped, I started feeling really empty. And hopeless, honestly, most days. It's just this feeling like I've already ruined my future in healthcare before it even really started.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this low, empty, or exhausted before in your life?

Not really before this, no. This whole feeling... the depressed, guilty, and just totally exhausted part, it's been going on for about nine months now. It basically started right after I crashed from that really high-energy period.
During that high-energy period you mentioned before you crashed, did you find that you needed much less sleep than usual to feel rested?

Yeah, I did. For a while back then, I could sleep for only two or three hours a night and still feel completely wired. Like I didn't need sleep at all. But lately... it's been really different. Now I either wake up way before dawn just feeling sick with worry, or I'll end up sleeping for half the day and still feel completely exhausted when I finally get up.

During these past nine months, have you felt so slowed down that other people noticed you were moving or speaking much more sluggishly than usual, or conversely, have you felt so restless that you couldn't sit still?

Yeah, actually. People at work have pointed it out to me. They said I looked really slowed down. And I... I could feel it, too. Just doing normal things, like putting a blood pressure cuff away or even just trying to answer a simple question, it would take me way longer than it normally does. It just felt like everything was in slow motion.
Are you currently able to perform your basic daily tasks at work or at home, or has this feeling of being slowed down made it impossible for you to function at your job?

No, I can't really function right now. It actually got to the point where I couldn't finish my documentation safely at work. I just couldn't stay focused on the patient-support tasks I'm supposed to do. Employee health eventually pulled me off the floor and sent me out for an emergency evaluation because of it. And at home... I was trying to study and prepare for my CNA certification, but I had to completely stop doing that, too. I just couldn't keep up with it anymore.
